ai.description: Beddome's toad is a small, 3–5 cm amphibian. It features a dark brown to black dorsum with a distinct, thin yellow mid-dorsal stripe and prominent parotoid glands. It belongs to the Bufonidae family.
ai.identificationRemarks: Beddome's Toad is best distinguished by the prominent, continuous, and highly elevated bony ridges that run along the top of its head, meeting to form a distinct "V" shape.
ai.habitat: Beddome's Toad inhabits the moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 700 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome's toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates across the leaf litter of its forest floor habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: Beddome's toad breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying eggs in long, gelatinous strings in shallow, stagnant water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: Beddome's toad is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka at elevations between 700 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: Beddome's Toad produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard near streams and rocky pools in the Western Ghats.
